note: Attacker-controlled bytes are wrapped in a KZip archive reader when the ORA handler parses the input stream.
The archive is opened on the same input device, so subsequent archive parsing consumes the attacker data.
While building the archive tree, nested path components are resolved recursively from archive entry names.
If a zero-length file already exists at a path that later needs to be treated as a directory, the old entry is removed from the parent directory and immediately freed.
A replacement directory object is inserted for the same name after the old entry has been deleted.
The directory map can still hold or return a stale pointer for the replaced name, creating a use-after-free hazard when later lookups traverse the entry tree.
The handler looks up the merged image entry after archive construction, and the lookup can dereference the stale freed directory entry chain.
The final sink reads through the archive file entry returned from the corrupted tree, triggering the heap-use-after-free read in the vulnerable target.
